answer.markdown:
**Boiler Feed Pump 101** (AST-BFP-101, NorthPlant Unit 1, criticality high): 32 alarm(s) in the last 90 days (5 critical, 27 high) from `get_alarms` / `summarize_alarms`.
Most frequent: **Low Suction Pressure** - 20 occurrences, 15% recurring within 24 h, average acknowledgement 184.6 s.
Weekly trend: increasing (13 -> 19 alarms, first vs second half).
Active now: Low Suction Pressure (high, unacknowledged).
Focus alarm ALM-002952 'Low Suction Pressure' scored 69.0 (P2).

**Likely contributing factors**
- **Deaerator 101: Deaerator Low Level leading to Low Suction Pressure** [high] - 'Deaerator Low Level' on related asset Deaerator 101 preceded 'Low Suction Pressure' 9 times (69% of source occurrences, avg lag 7.19 min, lift 2.46) (`correlate_alarms`) [S1] [S3]
- **BFP-101 Lube Oil Console: Low Lube Oil Pressure leading to High Bearing Temperature** [medium] - 'Low Lube Oil Pressure' on related asset BFP-101 Lube Oil Console preceded 'High Bearing Temperature' 2 times (67% of source occurrences, avg lag 8.07 min, lift 7.89) (`correlate_alarms`) [S2] [S5]
- **Boiler Feed Pump 101: Low Suction Pressure leading to Pump Trip** [medium] - 'Low Suction Pressure' on the same asset preceded 'Pump Trip' 4 times (20% of source occurrences, avg lag 5.38 min, lift 2.84) (`correlate_alarms`) [S1] [S3]
- **Recurring precursor: Boiler Feed Pump 102: Low Suction Pressure** [low] - Seen within 20 min before the alarm 1 time(s) in 90 days (`get_operator_recommendations`)
- **Chronic recurrence of 'Low Suction Pressure' (symptom of an unresolved upstream issue)** [medium] - 20 occurrences; 15% re-occurred within 24 h (`summarize_alarms`) [S4]
- **Alarm frequency is increasing over the window** [medium] - 13 alarms in first half vs 19 in second half (`get_alarm_trends`)

**Recommended actions (API, checked against documents)**
- **Do not follow as written** - Reset the pump trip and restart the pump immediately to restore feedwater flow _(immediate; CONFLICT with procedure)_ [S8] - Conflicts with documented restriction: "...restart the pump after a low suction pressure trip until deaerator level has been restored". The approved procedure takes precedence.
- Check deaerator level and pressure and restore level above 40% _(immediate; Consistent with procedure)_ [S1]
- Inspect the suction strainer differential pressure _(soon; Consistent with procedure)_ [S1]

**Procedure guidance**
- Verify that the minimum-flow recirculation valve FCV-103 is open when pump flow is low. [S1]
- If suction pressure continues to fall towards 2.8 bar(g), start the standby pump BFP-102 and reduce load on BFP-101 in coordination with the shift supervisor. [S1]

**Applicable documents**
- **SOP-BFP-001** rev 4.2 - Boiler Feed Pump Operation and Alarm Response Procedure: [S1] '3. Low Suction Pressure Alarm (BFP PT-001.LO)'; [S2] '5. High Bearing Temperature Alarm (TT-010.HI)'; [S4] '7. Recurring Alarms'; [S5] '1. Purpose and Scope'; [S8] '4. Pump Trip Response'
- **SOP-DEA-002** rev 2.0 - Deaerator Level Control and Low Level Response: [S3] '1. Purpose'; [S7] '4. Returning to Normal'
- **MM-BFP-010** rev 3.1 - Boiler Feed Pump Maintenance Manual - Bearings, Lubrication and Vibration: [S6] '3.1 High bearing temperature'

**Data gaps / degraded sources**
- `correlate_alarms` recovered after 1 retry(ies) (transient upstream error)

citations.title: Boiler Feed Pump Operation and Alarm Response Procedure
citations.snippet: Low suction pressure indicates a risk of cavitation. The most common causes, in order of frequency, are: low Deaerator 101 level, a partially blocked suction strainer, low deaerator pressure after a load change, and vapour formation caused by high feedwater temperature. citations.title: Deaerator Level Control and Low Level Response
citations.snippet: Deaerator 101 provides the suction head for Boiler Feed Pumps BFP-101 and BFP-102. Loss of deaerator level is the leading cause of low suction pressure alarms and boiler feed pump trips in Unit 1. This procedure describes the response to a Deaerator Low Level alarm (LT-001.LO, 40 %).

citations.title: Boiler Feed Pump Operation and Alarm Response Procedure
citations.snippet: If the same alarm occurs on a boiler feed pump more than three times in 24 hours, the shift supervisor must raise a reliability investigation. Recurring low suction pressure alarms are almost always caused by an upstream deaerator level control problem rather than a pump defect; the investigation must review Deaerator 101 level control performance and the level control valve.

citations.title: Boiler Feed Pump Operation and Alarm Response Procedure
citations.snippet: This procedure defines the operator response to alarms raised on Boiler Feed Pumps BFP-101 and BFP-102 in NorthPlant Unit 1. BFP-101 is normally the duty pump and BFP-102 the standby pump. Both pumps take suction from Deaerator 101 and are lubricated from the lube oil console LOS-101. The procedure applies to control room operators and field operators, and to shift supervisors who authorise pump restarts.

citations.title: Boiler Feed Pump Maintenance Manual - Bearings, Lubrication and Vibration
citations.snippet: Bearing temperature alarm is set at 85 degC and trip at 95 degC. On a high bearing temperature alarm: verify lube oil pressure and cooler outlet temperature, check oil for water contamination, and take an oil sample for particle count and water content. Increasing lube oil cooler water flow is acceptable as a temporary measure only when lube oil pressure is normal. Continued operation above 90 degC is not permitted; ...

citations.title: Deaerator Level Control and Low Level Response
citations.snippet: Level must be stable above 40 % for at least 10 minutes before any boiler feed pump that tripped on low suction pressure is restarted (see SOP-BFP-001 section 4).

citations.title: Boiler Feed Pump Operation and Alarm Response Procedure
citations.snippet: When a boiler feed pump trips, the standby pump starts automatically on low header pressure. The operator must confirm that the standby pump is running and that feedwater header pressure has recovered.
